title: Validate prerequisite refactor across integration and e2e coverage
description:
## Description
Run the validation pass for the prerequisite/bootstrap refactor, including building any required artifacts first, proving the shared prerequisite path works in a tool-ready environment, and proving missing-tool behavior fails with the intended diagnostic.

## Instructions
1. Run the required build/tooling preparation before dependent validation (`bun run build`, plus any other required preparation for changed test paths).
2. Run deterministic validation for the changed prerequisite/bootstrap paths, including `bun run validate:isolated-pins`, `bun test tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts`, `bun test tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts`, `bun test tests/e2e/additive-isolated-load.test.ts`, and `bun run test:launcher:preflight` as applicable.
3. Record pass/fail results and any intentional skips or conditional-tool cases.
4. Add at least one negative-path validation that deliberately removes a required tool from the host PATH (or otherwise simulates the missing-tool condition) and confirm the new explicit diagnostic fires instead of a downstream launcher/test failure.
5. Summarize validation evidence for acceptance review.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Required build/tooling preparation is run before dependent tests
- [ ] Relevant prerequisite/bootstrap coverage is executed and results are recorded
- [ ] At least one deliberate missing-tool validation confirms the explicit prerequisite diagnostic path
- [ ] Remaining blocked cases, if any, fail intentionally with explicit prerequisite diagnostics

title: Refactor duplicated test bootstrap and env setup code
description:
## Description
Refactor duplicated integration/e2e/manual-launcher bootstrap code so suites reuse shared prerequisite/bootstrap helpers instead of repeating binary lookup, PATH mutation, and local availability checks.

2. Eliminate the inline `checkBdAvailability` logic in manual-launcher integration coverage by routing through the shared prerequisite layer.
3. Share the stripped-env allowlist/bootstrap pieces currently split across launcher test env setup and manual-launcher preflight setup.
4. Keep suite-specific behavior explicit where needed, especially whether a verified host tool is intentionally exposed inside a generated isolated/manual test environment.
5. Limit this refactor to prerequisite/bootstrap duplication only; do not rewrite unrelated auth seeding, prewarm, or plugin-wiring logic in the large harness files.
6. After the shared path is in place, remove only the duplicated per-suite top-of-file availability/PATH setup and the inline `checkBdAvailability` code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Duplicated external-tool bootstrap code is reduced or removed from the affected suites
- [ ] Shared helpers own common host prerequisite and stripped-env bootstrap logic
- [ ] Suite-specific generated-env decisions remain explicit and readable
- [ ] Inline `checkBdAvailability` and repeated top-of-file availability/PATH setup are removed or consolidated
- [ ] Unrelated auth/prewarm/plugin-wiring logic is left intact

- tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts

title: Create shared host prerequisite checks for external test tools
description:
## Description
Create one shared host prerequisite layer for external test tools so integration/e2e/manual-launcher coverage verifies required binaries on the host machine before suite-specific environment setup begins.

## Instructions
1. Codify the host-tool contract for the targeted bootstrap paths: required `opencode` and `git`; conditional `aimgr` for aimgr-installed/additive coverage; conditional `bd` for beads bootstrap paths.
2. Extract a single host-binary resolver for PATH plus mise-based discovery instead of duplicating per-tool lookup logic.
3. Build a shared prerequisite helper on top of that resolver that reports resolved executable/bin-dir details and enforces required-vs-conditional tool policy.
4. Make missing required tools fail fast with a clear actionable diagnostic before deeper suite/bootstrap work begins.
5. The shared prerequisite helper must verify host availability and return resolution data; it must not mutate `process.env.PATH` implicitly and it must not inject tools into generated isolated/manual envs. Callers decide if and how resolved tools are added to runtime PATHs.
6. Update related test/docs entrypoints to use the shared prerequisite layer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shared helper defines the host-tool contract for the covered suites
- [ ] PATH/mise-based host binary resolution exists in one shared place
- [ ] Missing required tools produce a clear actionable failure message before deeper bootstrap occurs
- [ ] Shared prerequisite logic returns availability/resolution data without implicitly mutating host or generated-env PATH behavior

## Files to Modify
- tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts
- tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts
- tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts
- tests/e2e/additive-isolated-load.test.ts
- scripts/manual-test/preflight.ts
- docs/TESTING.md
close_reason: Implemented shared host prerequisite layer + resolver for e2e/integration/manual preflight; wired covered entrypoints and docs; validated with typecheck and targeted tests.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Specificity gap: instructions say 'inventory the externally required host tools' but don't name them. Why: without a fixed list, the implementer will re-debate scope mid-task. From the actual code the real list is: opencode (required by e2e + manual-launcher startup-viability), aimgr (required by aimgr-installed fixtures, optional elsewhere), bd (required only by beads-initialized fixture path), git (already implicitly required by createWorkspaceFromSource). Suggested action: pin this list in the task description and mark each as required/optional-per-suite so the helper API surface is decided up front.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Design ambiguity: acceptance criterion 4 says the shared check 'should not remove suite-specific control over generated environment PATH behavior'. Why this is unclear: today every suite does the same thing — prepends resolvedBinDir to process.env.PATH at module top-level. There is currently zero divergent PATH policy across suites. The user goal does say different tests may choose different generated-env PATH behavior afterward, but that refers to the generated isolated env (buildIsolatedPackageManagerEnv, launcher buildLauncherTestEnv), NOT process.env. Suggested action: clarify the boundary as 'shared check resolves host availability and returns resolvedBinDir; it does NOT mutate process.env.PATH and does NOT inject into generated isolated envs — each caller decides'. That is a real simplification, not just a contract.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Simplification opportunity: findExecutableOnPath + mise-latest probe + mise-installs scan is duplicated verbatim inside checkOpencodeAvailability, resolveOpencodeExecutablePath, and checkAimgrAvailability. Why: 3 copies of the same algorithm with only the binary name varying. Suggested action: extract one resolveHostBinary(name) -> { path, source: 'PATH'|'mise-latest'|'mise-scan' } and have all callers (including the new shared prereq helper and the existing prewarm path resolver) consume it. This is the actual win the user asked for; the prereq check is a thin wrapper on top.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Finding (HIGH): checkHostToolPrerequisites returns resolvedBinDir but no caller actually puts it on PATH. What: tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts, tests/e2e/opencode.test.ts, tests/e2e/additive-isolated-load.test.ts and scripts/manual-test/preflight.ts all just throw on missing-required and otherwise discard the resolution data. The previous per-file pattern was 'process.env.PATH = [check.resolvedBinDir, process.env.PATH].join(":")' and that mutation is gone. Why this matters: when opencode/aimgr/bd are resolved via mise-latest or mise-scan instead of PATH (opencodeCheck.source !== 'PATH'), every later subprocess (runLauncher, opencode SDK createOpencodeServer, aimgr install, bd init, opencode CLI in e2e) inherits the unmutated PATH and silently cannot find the binary. Today this only seems to work because in most dev environments the binaries also happen to be on PATH via mise shims, so the resolver hits source='PATH' and the missing prepend never manifests. Suggested action: either (a) make checkHostToolPrerequisites optionally prepend resolvedBinDir entries to process.env.PATH (opt-in flag), or (b) re-add an explicit prepend in each caller using the returned tools[]. Either way, the contract today is 'verified but not usable downstream' which is exactly the host-tool-resolution-vs-actual-usability hole the epic was supposed to close.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Finding (MED): checkOpencodeAvailability and checkAimgrAvailability are now thin redundant wrappers around resolveHostBinary that overlap with checkHostToolPrerequisites. Why: harness.ts still exports both per-tool helpers AND the new bulk helper, and both code paths are used (suites use checkHostToolPrerequisites, prewarm path uses resolveOpencodeExecutablePath, nothing uses checkOpencodeAvailability/checkAimgrAvailability anymore as far as I can see in the current diff). Suggested action: confirm via grep that checkOpencodeAvailability/checkAimgrAvailability have no remaining callers and delete them in opencode-coder-4vp; otherwise the 'one shared place' goal is half-done.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Finding (LOW): preflight runs checkHostToolPrerequisites BEFORE replacing HOME with tempHome, then spawns children with HOME=tempHome. What: scripts/manual-test/preflight.ts:48-55 checks prereqs against the real host HOME, but the spawned 'bun test tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts' child re-runs checkHostToolPrerequisites at top-level under HOME=tempHome — and resolveHostBinary uses env.HOME for mise-latest/mise-scan lookup. Why: if opencode is only available via mise (not real PATH), the parent says 'available' but the child says 'not available' and throws the diagnostic from the unrelated harness.ts file. This is a deterministic preflight failure mode hidden by the fact that on typical dev hosts opencode IS on PATH via the mise shim. Suggested action: pass the resolved executablePath / resolvedBinDir into the child env (or skip the child re-check) so the host check result actually reaches the spawned process.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Finding (LOW): scripts/manual-test/index.ts:724-730 has a useless ternary — both branches call createIsolatedOpenCodePaths with identical { prewarmOpenCodeData: true } options. What: 'openCodeBootstrapRequired ? createIsolatedOpenCodePaths(..., {prewarmOpenCodeData: true}) : createIsolatedOpenCodePaths(..., {prewarmOpenCodeData: true})'. Why: dead branch noise that will mislead future readers about whether non-bootstrap paths skip prewarm. Suggested action: collapse to a single call in the followup refactor task (4vp).

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Finding (LOW): manual-launcher.test.ts still defines its own buildLauncherTestEnv (PATH/USER/LOGNAME/LANG/LC_*) that duplicates BASE_ENV_KEYS in scripts/manual-test/preflight.ts. Why: the b0r task explicitly intended to consolidate this allowlist (per the planning comments on 4vp), and creating checkHostToolPrerequisites without also exposing a shared 'minimal stripped env' helper leaves the second half of the duplication intact. Suggested action: in 4vp, add a buildMinimalHostEnv helper in harness.ts so both files import the same allowlist.

title: Normalize external test-tool prerequisites and bootstrap
description:
## Description
Normalize external tool prerequisites for integration, e2e, and manual-launcher coverage so host-tool availability is checked once, failures are explicit, and suite bootstrap logic is shared instead of duplicated.

## Host Tool Contract
- Required host tools for the targeted bootstrap paths: `opencode`, `git`
- Conditionally required host tools: `aimgr` for aimgr-installed fixtures and additive install coverage; `bd` for beads-initialized fixture/bootstrap paths
- `bun` is not part of this prerequisite contract because these suites already run under Bun

## Policy
- Shared prerequisite logic must verify host availability and resolve the executable location in one place
- Shared prerequisite logic must not force one generated-env PATH policy on every suite; suites may still choose whether verified tools are exposed inside isolated/manual test environments
- Missing required host tools must fail fast with actionable diagnostics instead of surfacing later as downstream launcher/test failures

## Success Criteria
- [ ] External host tools required by the targeted bootstrap paths are explicitly defined and checked in one shared place
- [ ] Integration/e2e/manual-launcher suites use shared prerequisite/bootstrap helpers instead of duplicated per-file checks
- [ ] Missing required tools fail fast with clear diagnostics; optional/conditional tool behavior is intentional and explicit
- [ ] Validation includes both successful coverage in a tool-ready environment and at least one deliberate missing-tool diagnostic path
- [ ] Validation/build/test coverage for the refactor is captured in the acceptance review
close_reason: Epic complete: all implementation tasks closed (b0r, 4vp, cj3), acceptance review (4eh) passed. Feeder bug opencode-coder-mco subsumed.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Scope concern: success criterion #3 says missing tools should 'fail fast or skip intentionally with clear diagnostics'. Why this matters: 'fail fast OR skip' is two opposite policies and the user goal explicitly says 'fail when it is not [available]'. Today checkAimgrAvailability returns a soft warning, manual-launcher inlines a bd check that returns boolean for skipIf(), and checkOpencodeAvailability returns diagnostics but callers don't enforce. Suggested action: pick one policy per tool (required=fail, optional=skip-with-reason) and state it explicitly in the epic so b0r/4vp aren't free to re-introduce the current ambiguity.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Missing risk: 'bun' is listed as a required external tool but the suites already run under bun (process.execPath). Why: checking bun-on-PATH inside a bun process is theatre — it's guaranteed present. The real bun-related risk is the launcher spawning child shells without bun on PATH, which is a different problem (PATH propagation, not host availability). Suggested action: drop bun from the host-prereq list and, if PATH-propagation-to-children is a real concern, file it as a separate bug rather than folding it into this epic.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Relationship review: opencode-coder-mco is the directly related feeder bug for this epic and has been linked. opencode-coder-82u is adjacent bootstrap UX polish but stays standalone. opencode-coder-axu is a separate team-mode bd init timeout issue and stays standalone. opencode-coder-429 is unrelated lock/concurrency behavior found in nearby coverage and stays standalone.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Final review verdict: READY TO CLOSE. What: all four child tasks are in terminal states (b0r/4vp/cj3 closed; 4eh open as the acceptance review gate), the previously-flagged HIGH (PATH not propagated) and MED (redundant per-tool wrappers) findings on b0r are resolved in the current code, and cj3 records explicit positive-path runs (build, validate:isolated-pins, manual-launcher, opencode e2e, additive-isolated-load, launcher preflight) plus a deliberate negative-path run that surfaced the shared 'Missing required host tools for test bootstrap: opencode, bd' diagnostic instead of a downstream ENOENT. Why: this satisfies all five success criteria in the epic description (contract defined, shared helpers, fail-fast diagnostics, positive+negative validation, evidence captured). Suggested action: close the epic once 4eh is checked off; no further implementation work is required.

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Last concerns (non-blocking): (1) opencode-coder-btd intermittent installed-configured timeout — already filed as P3, did not reproduce in cj3 validation, network/cache-bound and pre-existing rather than introduced by b0r/4vp; acceptable to defer. (2) Residual LOW from cj3 review: scripts/manual-test/preflight.ts relies on parent PATH propagation reaching the spawned 'bun test' child rather than passing resolved bin dirs explicitly; works today because the prepended PATH is inherited, but the child's mise-scan branch is effectively dead under preflight. Why it's non-blocking: behavior is correct on tool-ready hosts and the negative-path diagnostic still fires; only matters on hosts where opencode is exclusively mise-resolvable and not on PATH. Suggested action: if you want to be tidy, file a P3 follow-up to either document the parent-PATH-propagation contract in preflight.ts or pass resolved bin dirs into the child env — but do not block the epic close on it.

title: Core init workflow split across hidden reference breaks Phase 2 continuation
description:
## Discovered in
Manual Phase 2 continuation review on 2026-04-18 after a successful Phase 1 install/restart flow.

## Problem
The resource-backed `/opencode-coder/init` command tells the model to "Initialize and set up opencode-coder for this project", but the actual setup workflow is split across `coder-core` references in a way that makes the continuation path easy to miss.

Observed behavior:
- The command loads `coder-core`.
- The model naturally reads `references/installation-setup.md` and `references/mode-runtime.md`.
- It does **not** naturally read `references/init-dispatch.md`.
- As a result, Phase 2 continuation after restart can stall even when the project is installed correctly.

Why this happens:
- `init-dispatch.md` is really part of installation/setup, not a distinct concept.
- `coder-core/SKILL.md` currently lists both `installation-setup.md` and `init-dispatch.md` under the same top-level workflow, which hides the real instruction path instead of making it obvious.
- The command file is too thin to force the model toward the missing reference.

## Expected
The core installation/setup reference should directly include the setup-continuation workflow so that when the command says "Initialize and set up opencode-coder for this project", the model naturally reads the right reference and continues setup.

## Actual
The continuation/setup logic is isolated in `ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/init-dispatch.md`, which the model can skip.

## Fix direction
- Merge the useful workflow content from `references/init-dispatch.md` into `references/installation-setup.md`.
- Remove the separate `init-dispatch.md` concept.
- Update `coder-core/SKILL.md` so the top-level setup workflow points to the right core setup references without the hidden extra file.
- Update any tests that currently protect the split-file structure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `installation-setup.md` includes the setup-continuation workflow currently isolated in `init-dispatch.md`
- [ ] `init-dispatch.md` is removed
- [ ] `coder-core/SKILL.md` no longer references a separate init-dispatch file
- [ ] `/opencode-coder/init` command wording remains simple while naturally leading the model to the right setup reference
- [ ] Related tests are updated

## Files to Modify
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/SKILL.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/installation-setup.md
- ai-resources/skills/coder-core/references/init-dispatch.md
- tests/unit/docs-lifecycle-contract.test.ts
close_reason: Merged continuation workflow into installation-setup.md, removed init-dispatch.md, and updated tests.

title: Phase 2 init does not resume cleanly after successful Phase 1 restart
description:
## Discovered in
User manual validation of `opencode-coder-bsr` on 2026-04-18.

## Expected
After Phase 1 succeeds in an empty project, closing and reopening OpenCode should allow the user to run `/opencode-coder/init` again and continue into the resource-backed init flow cleanly.

## Actual
Phase 1 worked, but after closing OpenCode and restarting it, the user could not really continue with Phase 2.

## Repro
1. Start OpenCode in an empty project.
2. Run `/opencode-coder/init` and complete Phase 1 successfully.
3. Close OpenCode.
4. Reopen OpenCode in the same project.
5. Try to continue with `/opencode-coder/init`.
6. Observe that Phase 2 does not resume cleanly.

## Impact
This blocks the intended two-step init flow even when Phase 1 succeeds. The standard setup experience is incomplete until restart/continuation works reliably.

## Notes needed
Need follow-up triage to capture the exact post-restart behavior:
- was `/opencode-coder/init` missing?
- did Phase 1 bootstrap show again instead of the resource-backed command?
- did command execution fail?
- were installed surfaces missing or not detected?

## Related Work

comments.author: Hans Kohlreiter
comments.text: Assessment (likely real but not a regression): the timed-out test 'supports installed-configured plugin source with deterministic package prep' (or the viability variant) runs prepareWorkspacePluginSource → installWorkspacePluginDependencies → 'bun add --exact @hk9890/opencode-dynatrace@0.6.0 @dynatrace-oss/opencode-coder@...' against npm + GitHub Packages, plus opencode server startup. Why intermittent: the 'bun add' step is network-bound (GitHub Packages + npm registry); 120000ms is a tight ceiling when the registry is cold or rate-limited. Evidence in code: tests/integration/manual-launcher.test.ts installed-configured tests all set timeout 120000; harness.ts:643 spawns 'bun add --exact <specs>' with no retry. Recommended next steps: (1) confirm by checking whether the failing run was the first time NODE_AUTH_TOKEN/registry was hit on that host, (2) raise installed-configured test timeouts to 240000ms, (3) consider a one-time warm-cache step in preflight for the pinned specs so subsequent suites use the cache, (4) NOT a blocker for closing wk0 — file as P3 unless it recurs in CI. Note: the bug is unlikely to be caused by the b0r refactor itself; the network-install path was already there. But verify by re-running preflight twice in a row on a clean Bun cache to confirm the cache-warm hypothesis.
